references.title: Activity first, facts close by
references.observation: Saved Ride evidence: dark activity masthead, asymmetric action hero, followed by performance merchandise and brand stories.
references.problem: A recreational buyer needs a relevant activity route before choosing an equipment-specific option.
references.retained: A clear primary CTA, activity context and contained shopping navigation.
references.difference: Trailmark opens three named activity pathways and follows with a light factual merchandising area. It avoids relying on action imagery to communicate measurements.
references.contract: A category navigation and product primitives; C activity bindings and equipment-card facts.

references.title: Measured facts without implied compatibility
references.observation: Saved Tinker evidence: selected mechanical puzzle uses concise dimension tiles beside a conventional purchase area. The saved screenshot has an unloaded gallery; that is an evidence limit.
references.problem: A buyer needs actual dimensions and clear absent fit information, even when photography is attractive.
references.retained: Readable dimensions, units and a conventional purchase flow.
references.difference: Trailmark groups racket length, unstrung mass, grip circumference, supplied use conditions and unconfirmed replacement compatibility. Clothing uses a separate attribute model.
references.contract: C typed category facts, public projection and unit validation; D source responsibility for compatibility claims.
